 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Rajiv Roy
 Oral Order
4 02-02-2026 Heard the parties.

2. The present petition has been preferred for the following relief/s:
(i) for setting aside the order dated 27.07.2018 passed by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Patna Flood Protection Project, Patna, whereby the application filed Patna High Court CWJC No.20586 of 2019(4) dt.02-02-2026 by the petitioners Satya Narayan Tandon, vs The State Of Bihar on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171960743/
1 under section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 claiming payment of compensation in accordance with the award dated 30.06.2000 passed in Land Acquisition Case No. 6/92/489/92 (Sargun Singh and others Vs. The State
), was rejected on wrong assumption of facts and law.

(ii) For holding that the reasons assigned for rejecting the application of the petitioners filed under section 28A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 that the claim as per the order of the court as aforesaid, was made after three months of such order is wrong inasmuch as the impugned order dated 27.07.2008 itself says that the application, though contains the signature of the Advocate of the petitioners made on 29.09.2000, but the said application does not contain the signature of any clerk or officer with date.
Thus inspite of there being an application made within three months of the award the rejection of the application is totally wrong and illegal.

(iii) For holding that the award amount/compensation for acquisition of the lands of the petitioners cannot be withheld or Patna High Court CWJC No.20586 of 2019(4) dt.02-02-2026 refused on technical grounds and the same has to be paid to the landowner/beneficiary in any case.
(iv) For holding that the impugned order as contained in Annexure-1 is inequitable, prejudicial in effect causing sever loss and prejudice to the petitioners.
(v) For grant of any such other relief or reliefs, for which the petitioners are legally entitled in the facts and circumstances of this case.
2 . On 07.01.2026, notices were issued to respondent nos. 4 to 7 and the order was peremptory.

3. As the same was not complied, it stood rejected on 21.01.2026.
4.
Perused the file, consigned.

(Rajiv Roy, J) Ravi/-
